rules.title: S.2983 – An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting
rules.requirement: Pending Senate bill that would prohibit algorithmic rent setting. It was reported favorably by the Housing Committee on 3/12/2026 and sent to Senate Ways and Means. It is not law, and the page does not show its operative text.
rules.key_value: pending ban on algorithmic rent setting
rules.quoted_span: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting
rules.effective_date_note: Pending bill; no effective date. Bill text not shown on the page.
rules.interaction: New draft of S.994 and S.1016; companion to House bill H.5222.

rules.title: H.5222 – An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market
rules.requirement: Pending House bill on algorithmic rent fixing in rental housing. It was reported favorably by the Housing Committee on 3/12/2026 and sent to House Ways and Means. It is not law, and the page does not give its operative text.
rules.key_value: pending bill on algorithmic rent fixing
rules.quoted_span: An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market

rules.title: State prohibition on local rent control
rules.requirement: Massachusetts cities and towns may not enact, maintain or enforce rent control. Only a voluntary, municipally-compensated scheme for owners of ten or more units with fair market rent of $400 or less is allowed.
rules.key_value: Statewide ban on local rent control
rules.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides:
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date (known to stem from 1994 ballot Question 9).
rules.exemptions: A city or town accepting the chapter may adopt voluntary rent control compensated from general funds, only for owners of ten or more units and units with fair market rent of $400 or less.
rules.conflict_note: State bar may preempt local rent control ordinances in any MA city; flag for human review.

rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21 – statewide rent increase cap (blocked from ballot)
rules.requirement: The proposed initiative would have repealed the state ban on rent control and capped annual rent increases at the lesser of CPI or 5%. The SJC ruled in June 2026 it cannot appear on the November 2026 ballot, so it is not law.
rules.key_value: lesser of CPI or 5% annual cap (not enacted)
rules.quoted_span: Under the proposed law, annual rent increases would have been limited to the lesser of the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index or 5%
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, units less than 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, educational/religious/nonprofit facilities.
rules.conflict_note: Proponents say the defect is easily fixable and may re-file (possibly 2028); no rent cap in force.

rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment under a written lease
rules.requirement: For nonpayment of rent under a written lease, a landlord may end the lease with a 14-day written notice to quit. The tenant can stop termination by paying all rent due, interest and costs by the answer day in an eviction case.
rules.key_value: 14 days' written notice to quit; right to cure
rules.quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.

rules.title: Notice to determine estate at will
rules.requirement: A tenancy at will ends with three months' written notice (or the rental interval/30 days if longer). For nonpayment, 14 days' notice to quit applies, and a tenant without a similar notice in the prior 12 months can stop termination by paying all rent due within 10 days.
rules.key_value: 3 months' notice; 14 days for nonpayment; 10-day cure
rules.quoted_span: In case of neglect or refusal to pay the rent due from a tenant at will, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the tenancy;
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.

unverifiable_exemptions: tenancy must be at will (not a fixed-term lease)

rules.title: Reprisal protections for tenants who report violations or organize
rules.requirement: A landlord may not threaten or take reprisals against a tenant for enforcing housing laws, reporting code violations or joining a tenants' union. A termination notice (other than for nonpayment), rent increase or substantial change in terms within six months of such activity is presumed a reprisal.
rules.key_value: Damages of 1-3 months' rent or actual damages; 6-month rebuttable presumption
rules.quoted_span: shall create a rebuttable presumption that such notice or other action is a reprisal against the tenant for engaging in such activities
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.
rules.penalty: Damages of 1 to 3 months' rent or actual damages if greater, plus costs and reasonable attorney's fees

rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment: required state form
rules.requirement: A written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent must be accompanied by the state form listing rental assistance and legal protections and stating it is not an eviction. Courts will not accept a summary process filing for nonpayment without proof the form was delivered.
rules.key_value: State form must accompany nonpayment notice to quit
rules.quoted_span: No court having jurisdiction over an action for summary process pursuant to chapter 239, including the Boston municipal court department, shall, in an eviction for nonpayment of rent for a residential dwelling unit, accept for filing a writ, summons or complaint without proof of delivery of the form required under this section
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.

rules.title: Security deposit limits and handling
rules.requirement: A landlord may not require a security deposit above the first month's rent. The deposit must be held in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts account with a receipt and statement of condition, pay 5% interest (or bank rate if lower), and be returned within 30 days after tenancy ends less itemized lawful deductions.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent cap; return within 30 days; 5% interest
rules.quoted_span: a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3) and that the tenant is given the statement of condition as required by subsection (2)
rules.effective_date_note: Original effective date not stated; 2025 amendment (eff. 2025-08-01) added agents and a possible fee in lieu of deposit via regulations.
rules.exemptions: Leases of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.penalty: Forfeiture of right to retain deposit; treble damages plus 5% interest, costs and attorney's fees for certain violations.

unverifiable_exemptions: vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less

rules.title: Limit on upfront charges at lease start (no application or screening fees by landlords)
rules.requirement: At or before the start of a tenancy, a landlord (or agent, from Aug 1, 2025) may require only first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of no more than one month's rent, and the cost of a key and lock. Application and screening fees charged by landlords are not allowed.
rules.key_value: Only first month, last month, deposit (max 1 month), key/lock cost
rules.quoted_span: At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:
rules.effective_date_note: Limit on lessors predates 2025 (secondary source says since the 1970s); the extension to agents took effect 2025-08-01.
rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less. Licensed brokers' fees are governed separately.

unverifiable_exemptions: vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less

rules.conflict_note: Secondary source D054 says brokers may charge application fees under 254 CMR 7; landlord-as-broker status is uncertain.

rules.title: Broker fee allocation: only the party who engaged the broker pays
rules.requirement: A licensed broker may contract with either the tenant or the landlord, not both for the same deal. Any broker fee must be paid only by the party who originally hired the broker.
rules.key_value: Broker fee paid only by the party who engaged the broker
rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson
rules.effective_date_note: Amended text effective August 1, 2025 per 2025, 9, Sec. 136 as stated on the page.

rules.title: Ban on discrimination against public assistance and housing subsidy recipients
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate against someone because they receive public assistance or a housing subsidy such as a voucher, or because of a requirement of that program. Other subsections bar refusing to rent or asking about protected characteristics.
rules.key_value: ban on discrimination against public assistance / housing subsidy recipients
rules.quoted_span: For any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations to discriminate against any individual who is a recipient of federal, state, or local public assistance, including medical assistance, or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements, because the individual is such a recipient
rules.effective_date_note: The document does not give an effective date for subsection 10.
rules.exemptions: Subsection 7 excludes leasing a single apartment in a two-family dwelling occupied by the owner.

unverifiable_exemptions: Subsection 7 does not apply to a single apartment in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling

no_rule_findings.finding: No enacted Massachusetts state law bans algorithmic rent setting as of the query date; bills are pending in the House and Senate.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: Bills banning the practice in the rental market are also working their way through the Massachusetts state House and Senate

parsed.notes: Merged S.2983 candidates and the two ballot-initiative candidates. The G.L. c. 186, § 15B upfront-charge candidates are merged into one record. The 254 C.M.R. 7 broker disclosure candidate (c97) was dropped because it comes from a secondary source only. The link-only CORI housing regulation (D056) was not added because no provided document supports it. Original effective dates for the c. 40P and § 15B provisions are not stated in the documents, so they are left null.
